business_problem: Using MongoDB Atlas to enhance an AI-powered platform for Element451 According to the World Economic Forum, Powerful AI applications can help educational institutions serve their communities by streamlining tasks and increasing engagement.
solution_summary: Using MongoDB Atlas to enhance an AI-powered platform for Element451 According to the World Economic Forum, Powerful AI applications can help educational institutions serve their communities by streamlining tasks and increasing engagement. Powering more than 100,000 AI conversations Element451 planned its migration to MongoDB Atlas independently, then optimized its strategy with help from the MongoDB Atlas team. Using MongoDB, Element451 developed an advanced AI platform, improved flexibility, and scaled by 80% year over year — all with the aim of helping higher education organizations reach students more effectively. Now, Element451 uses AI to provide tools and technology to administrative teams to manage communication and data across the student journey — from marketing to prospective students to keeping in touch with alumni. “Using SQL, we needed to preplan everything,” said Petar Djordjevic, chief technology officer at Element451.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
solution_components.role: Retrieves semantically relevant context from Element451's data for AI, search, and recommendation workflows.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas Search
solution_components.role: Provides relevance-based text retrieval across Element451's documents and application data.

solution_components.name: Atlas Search Nodes
solution_components.role: Separates search compute from the operational database so Element451 can scale search independently.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores the operational, document, and context data behind Element451's customer-service and assistant workflows.

data_flow: Business documents, tickets, records, and other operational content stay in MongoDB Atlas Vector Search and MongoDB Atlas Search, where search indexes or vector embeddings are built and then queried in real time to supply grounded results to applications, assistants, or discovery features. Upstream and downstream integrations include AWS, CRM systems.
business_outcome: Achieving growth for Element451 and its customers Since first adopting MongoDB, Element451 has scaled from 15 customers to more than 200, an 80% year-over-year growth since 2020.
metrics: After adopting Search Nodes, the team saw CPU usage go from almost complete saturation to 30% to 40% usage during peak hours, while average execution times improved by 10X, dropping down to 10 to 20 milliseconds.

The company’s customers have had more than 100,000 conversations with AI assistants in less than one year, which lightened the load on teachers and administrators and reduced call volume for some customers by 14%.
Element451’s database processes 70,000 jobs per minute, and it has helped institutions complete 2 million tasks and process more than 1 million admission applications.
By taking advantage of the flexibility and scalability of MongoDB Atlas, the company’s developer team also rolled out more than 1,200 updates, including brand-new features and tools, in only a year.
The AI-powered bots on the platform even reduced call volume by 14% through efficient inquiry management, saving the college’s staff more than 36,000 minutes.
architecture_clues: The migration approach minimized or avoided downtime during cutover.
Vector search is part of the retrieval layer for semantic or generative-AI use cases.
AI agents or assistants are layered on top of the MongoDB data platform.
The deployment integrates with CRM systems.
